subject: Machine learning: from backpropagation and minimax to RLHF and RLVR

concepts.label: Linear algebra basics
concepts.description: Vectors, matrices, dot products and matrix multiplication.

concepts.label: Derivatives
concepts.description: How a function's output changes as its input changes.

concepts.label: Partial derivatives and gradients
concepts.description: Derivatives of multivariable functions; the gradient points uphill.

concepts.label: Chain rule
concepts.description: Differentiating a composition by multiplying the derivatives of its parts.

concepts.label: Probability basics
concepts.description: Random variables, distributions and their rules.

concepts.label: Expectation and variance
concepts.description: Average value of a random variable and its spread.

concepts.label: Conditional probability
concepts.description: Probability of an event given another; Bayes' rule.

concepts.label: Maximum likelihood estimation
concepts.description: Fitting parameters by maximising the (log) probability of observed data.

concepts.label: Entropy and cross-entropy
concepts.description: Expected surprise of a distribution; cross-entropy compares two distributions.

concepts.label: KL divergence
concepts.description: How far one probability distribution is from another (not symmetric).

concepts.label: Softmax
concepts.description: Turns a vector of scores into a probability distribution.

concepts.label: Monte Carlo estimation
concepts.description: Estimating an expectation by averaging random samples.

concepts.label: Importance sampling
concepts.description: Estimating an expectation under one distribution with samples from another, reweighted by their ratio.

concepts.label: Supervised learning
concepts.description: Learning a function from labelled input-output examples.

concepts.label: Loss functions
concepts.description: A number that measures how wrong a model's predictions are.

concepts.label: Gradient descent
concepts.description: Minimising a loss by repeatedly stepping against its gradient.

concepts.label: Learning rate
concepts.description: How big each gradient-descent step is.

concepts.label: Stochastic gradient descent
concepts.description: Gradient descent using gradients estimated from small random batches.

concepts.label: Momentum and Adam
concepts.description: Optimisers that smooth and rescale gradient steps.

concepts.label: Linear regression
concepts.description: Fitting a linear function by minimising squared error.

concepts.label: Logistic regression
concepts.description: Binary classification with a sigmoid of a linear score, trained with cross-entropy.

concepts.label: Overfitting and regularization
concepts.description: Fitting training data too closely, and the penalties and checks that prevent it.

concepts.label: Activation functions
concepts.description: Nonlinear functions (ReLU, tanh, sigmoid) applied between layers.

concepts.label: Neural networks
concepts.description: Layers of linear maps and nonlinearities composed into one model.

concepts.label: Computational graphs
concepts.description: A computation written as a graph of simple operations.

concepts.label: Backpropagation
concepts.description: Computing all gradients of a loss by applying the chain rule backwards through the graph.

concepts.label: Convolutional neural networks
concepts.description: Networks that share weights across positions with convolutions.

concepts.label: Recurrent neural networks
concepts.description: Networks that process sequences step by step with a hidden state.

concepts.label: Embeddings
concepts.description: Learned vectors that represent discrete items such as tokens.

concepts.label: Residual connections
concepts.description: Adding a layer's input to its output so deep networks train.

concepts.label: Normalization layers
concepts.description: Rescaling activations inside a network to stabilise training.

concepts.label: Search algorithms
concepts.description: Systematically exploring states to reach a goal.

concepts.label: Adversarial search
concepts.description: Search over the moves of two players with opposing goals.

concepts.label: Minimax
concepts.description: Choose the move that maximises your worst-case outcome against an optimal opponent.

concepts.label: Alpha-beta pruning
concepts.description: Skipping minimax branches that cannot change the decision.

concepts.label: Expectimax
concepts.description: Minimax with chance nodes that average over random outcomes.

concepts.label: Reinforcement learning
concepts.description: Learning to act from rewards by trial and error.

concepts.label: Multi-armed bandits
concepts.description: Choosing between actions with unknown rewards; the explore/exploit trade-off.

concepts.label: Markov decision processes
concepts.description: States, actions, transition probabilities and rewards: the formal RL problem.

concepts.label: Policy
concepts.description: The agent's rule for choosing actions in each state.

concepts.label: Return and discounting
concepts.description: The (discounted) sum of future rewards an agent tries to maximise.

concepts.label: Value functions
concepts.description: Expected return from a state when following a policy.

concepts.label: Action-value function
concepts.description: Expected return after taking an action in a state, then following the policy.

concepts.label: Bellman equations
concepts.description: Recursive equations linking a state's value to its successors' values.

concepts.label: Value iteration and policy iteration
concepts.description: Solving a known MDP by repeated Bellman backups.

concepts.label: Temporal-difference learning
concepts.description: Updating value estimates from sampled one-step transitions and bootstrapped targets.

concepts.label: Q-learning
concepts.description: Learning action values off-policy with TD updates.

concepts.label: Deep Q-networks
concepts.description: Q-learning with a neural network, replay buffer and target network.

concepts.label: Policy gradient
concepts.description: Improving a parameterised policy by gradient ascent on expected return, using the log-probability trick.

concepts.label: REINFORCE
concepts.description: The basic policy-gradient algorithm: weight each action's log-probability by its return.

concepts.label: Baselines and variance reduction
concepts.description: Subtracting a state-dependent baseline from returns to reduce policy-gradient variance.

concepts.label: Advantage function
concepts.description: How much better an action is than the policy's average in that state: A = Q - V.

concepts.label: Generalized advantage estimation
concepts.description: Estimating advantages from TD errors with an exponentially weighted (lambda) average.

concepts.label: Actor-critic
concepts.description: A policy (actor) trained with advantages from a learned value function (critic).

concepts.label: Trust region policy optimization
concepts.description: Policy updates constrained to a KL trust region around the old policy.

concepts.label: Proximal policy optimization
concepts.description: Actor-critic updates that clip the new/old policy probability ratio to keep steps small.

concepts.label: Tokenization
concepts.description: Splitting text into the discrete units a language model reads.

concepts.label: Language modeling
concepts.description: Predicting the next token's probability given previous tokens; trained by maximum likelihood.

concepts.label: Attention
concepts.description: Mixing token representations with softmax weights from query-key similarity.

concepts.label: Transformers
concepts.description: Stacks of attention and MLP blocks with residuals and normalisation.

concepts.label: Large language models
concepts.description: Transformer language models pretrained on large text corpora.

concepts.label: Decoding and sampling
concepts.description: Generating text from a language model's next-token distribution.

concepts.label: Fine-tuning
concepts.description: Continuing to train a pretrained model on task-specific data.

concepts.label: Supervised fine-tuning
concepts.description: Fine-tuning a language model on demonstration responses with the next-token loss.

concepts.label: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning
concepts.description: Fine-tuning a small set of added parameters instead of the whole model.

concepts.label: Preference data
concepts.description: People choosing which of two model responses is better.

concepts.label: Bradley-Terry model
concepts.description: Models P(A preferred to B) as a sigmoid of the score difference.

concepts.label: Reward models
concepts.description: A language model fine-tuned to score responses, trained on preference pairs.

concepts.label: RL fine-tuning of language models
concepts.description: Treating a language model as a policy whose actions are tokens and optimising a reward with policy gradients.

concepts.label: Reward hacking
concepts.description: The policy exploiting flaws in the reward signal instead of doing the intended task.

concepts.label: KL penalty to a reference model
concepts.description: Penalising divergence from the starting model to limit reward hacking and drift.

concepts.label: Reinforcement learning from human feedback
concepts.description: SFT, then a reward model from human preferences, then PPO fine-tuning against it with a KL penalty.

concepts.label: Direct preference optimization
concepts.description: Optimising the policy directly on preference pairs without a separate reward model or RL loop.

concepts.label: Verifiable rewards
concepts.description: Rewards computed by a program that checks the answer, e.g. a math checker or unit tests.

concepts.label: Group relative policy optimization
concepts.description: PPO-style updates whose baseline is the mean reward of a group of samples for the same prompt, with no critic.

concepts.label: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards
concepts.description: RL fine-tuning of a language model against automatically checkable rewards instead of a learned reward model.
